title: A Simple Home-based Ring Test May Promote Early Diagnosis of Retinal Detachment, Retinal Vascular Diseases and Common Optic Nerve Disease.
abstract: Background and objective The purpose of this study was to evaluate a simple ring-based visual field screening test to determine whether, when used at home, the findings were similar to clinical evaluation in terms of visual field defects associated with retinal and optic nerve diseases. Patients and methods This was a prospective observational cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy study. Consecutive patients presenting between May 2023 and February 2025 with acute vision loss, known history of retinal or optic nerve disorders, or symptoms of acute posterior vitreous detachment or floaters were enrolled. A total of 594 patients (667 eyes) were included. With the fellow eye occluded, patients viewed a 360° ring target and reported any missing or distorted segments. Ring-test findings were compared with clinical reference standards including dilated fundus examination, fundus photography, and Humphrey Visual Field (HVF) testing. Concordance between ring test defects and HVF defects was assessed based on location and orientation. Results Of a total of 667 eyes, 240 eyes underwent HVF testing. Among 88 eyes with HVF defects, the ring test identified 80 (sensitivity, 0.91; 95% CI, 0.83-0.96). Among 152 eyes without HVF defects, 149 were correctly classified (specificity, 0.98; 95% CI, 0.94-1.00). Ring test findings demonstrated strong spatial concordance with clinical pathology. Conclusions Concordance between ring test defects and HVF defects was high, with strong sensitivity and specificity for detecting mid-to-peripheral visual field defects in rhegmatogenous retinal detachment, retinal vascular occlusions, and certain optic neuropathies. Preliminary results of this initial proof-of-concept study suggest that the ring test has potential utility as a home-based screening tool to facilitate earlier awareness of vision-threatening conditions. Further studies are needed to evaluate its role in routine clinical practice.

title: Aberrant cortical reorganization and astrogliosis underlie memory deficit post-traumatic brain injury: a longitudinal multiscale multimodal study
abstract: Integrating high-dimensional neuroimaging data across spatial scales remains a fundamental bottleneck in quantitative neuroscience. Here, we apply emerging analytical techniques including functional connectome gradient mapping and 3D segmentation of whole-brain cellular resolution microscopy data in a mouse model of traumatic brain injury. At the macroscale, longitudinal functional MRI revealed a transition from frontal hyperconnectivity to hippocampal hypoconnectivity and unimodal-transmodal gradient contraction indicating network dedifferentiation. At the cellular scale, deep-learning based segmentation of whole-brain light-sheet fluorescence microscopy volumes quantified regional astrogliosis, neuronal hyperactivity, and single-axon loss undetected by standard diffusion MRI. Multiscale multimodal data integration not only identified quantitative biomarkers predictive of memory performance post-injury but also enabled validation of in vivo modalities against more sensitive ex vivo histology. This study demonstrates a framework for probing complex multi-network cognitive functions and neurological disorders of network dysfunction.

title: Anatomically Programmable and Optically Tunable 3D-Bioprinted Tumor-Mimicking Phantoms for Quantitative Nanofluorophore Benchmarking
abstract: Surgical resection remains a primary treatment for solid tumors, with fluorescence-guided surgery offering improved intraoperative visualization and precision. However, conventional murine models provide limited control over anatomical and optical variables critical to evaluating fluorescent imaging agents. Here, we developed 3D-bioprinted, anatomically tailored and optically tunable tumor-mimicking phantoms (TMPs) as a reproducible platform for quantitative nanofluorophore evaluation under tissue-relevant surgical conditions. These TMPs recreate subcutaneous, epithelial, and intraperitoneal tumor presentations while enabling controlled variation of lesion geometry, spatial distribution, tissue pigmentation, cellular composition, and nanofluorophore concentration. Semiconducting polymer nanofluorophores (SPNs) with distinct emission profiles were incorporated as model imaging agents and evaluated using an in vivo imaging system (IVIS). The engineered phantoms enabled quantitative assessment of wavelength-dependent fluorescence, lesion visualization and delineation across diverse geometries and tissue backgrounds, multiplexed imaging of spatially distinct lesions, and simulation of fluorescence-guided tumor resection. Constructs incorporating GFP-expressing cancer cells further demonstrated simultaneous visualization of cellular and nanoprobe-derived fluorescence. Collectively, these findings establish anatomically programmable TMPs as a versatile, reproducible framework for benchmarking fluorescent imaging agents, systematically interrogating anatomical and optical determinants of imaging performance, and advancing fluorescence-guided surgical strategies before in vivo evaluation and clinical translation.

title: Development of a deep learning model for glomerulus detection and segmentation in kidney histopathology images
abstract: Background: Estimation of nephron number, an indicator of renal reserve, requires quantitative assessment of glomerular number and size in kidney biopsy specimens. We aimed to develop an automated system for quantitative measurement of glomerular areas from clinical kidney biopsy images, across diverse kidney diseases. Methods: We developed a two-stage deep learning system combining Faster R-CNN for glomerular detection in whole-slide images (WSIs) and DeepLabV3+ for segmentation. Of 114 kidney biopsies (228 WSIs), 104 were used for model development and 10 for independent final evaluation. Agreement was assessed using the F1-score for detection, the Dice coefficient for segmentation, and the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) for glomerular area measurement. Analysis was performed at 40× total magnification (2.331 μm/pixel) and validated against 400× images. Results: In the independent evaluation set, the artificial intelligence (AI) model achieved a mean F1-score of 0.851 for detection, compared with 0.888 among experts. For segmentation, the Dice coefficient was 0.959 ± 0.011 and the per-pair ICC (2,1) for area measurement was 0.989 ± 0.009; both were comparable to inter-expert agreement. Bland–Altman analysis showed a mean bias of −344 μm 2 (95% limits of agreement, −1904 to 1216 μm 2 ) between 40× and 400× measurements. Conclusion: The two-stage model achieved glomerular segmentation and area measurement comparable to expert agreement in independent clinical data, with detection performance approaching inter-expert agreement, and provided reliable measurements at low magnification. This automated approach may facilitate large-scale quantitative kidney pathology and nephron number estimation from clinical kidney biopsies.

title: Ordinal Multi-Instance Learning for Automated Multi-Task Grading of Lumbar Degenerative Conditions on Sagittal MRI, with External Validation
abstract: Purpose: Lumbar spine MRI interpretation requires 25 structured severity judgments per examination (five degenerative conditions at five disc levels, each on a three-level ordinal scale), a time-consuming task with substantial inter-reader variability. We developed and externally validated a model that automates this complete scheme. Materials and Methods: A full-sequence multi-instance learning (MIL) model (ResNet34 backbone, bidirectional GRU, attention pooling over 24 uniformly sampled sagittal T2-weighted slices) with 25 cumulative-logit ordinal heads was trained on 1,204 examinations from the multi-institutional RSNA 2024 LumbarDISC dataset and internally validated on 213 held-out examinations. External validation used 60 retrospectively collected patients from an independent Chinese university hospital (four scanner vendors, radiology reports as the reference standard, no fine-tuning). Agreement was assessed with exact accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, McNemar tests, and patient-clustered bootstrap confidence intervals. Results: The ordinal model achieved 51.4% balanced accuracy internally (exact accuracy 65.1%), versus 16.3% for a single-slice baseline; severe-grade AUCs averaged 0.908 across conditions. Externally, it outperformed its softmax-weighted counterpart on exact accuracy (0.649 vs. 0.586; +6.3 percentage points, 95% CI +2.7 to +10.0) and sensitivity (0.868 vs. 0.833), with markedly fewer severe-grade false alarms (69 vs. 172 predicted severe cells; McNemar p<0.0001). Conclusion: A full-sequence MIL model with ordinal outputs automates the complete 25-task grading scheme on sagittal MRI and, in the first hospital external validation of such a model, reduced severe-grade over-prediction under domain shift without loss of sensitivity, supporting its role as a screening and triage aid.

title: ReSeg: Retraining-free segmentation of abdominal organs via generalizable semantic representation learning
abstract: Abdominal organ segmentation is essential in modern medical applications. While existing deep learning approaches demonstrate promising performance, their heavy reliance on large-scale image data raises concerns over generalization capability and privacy risks. This motivates the development of generalizable segmentation training paradigms based on domain-randomized image synthesis, facilitating generalization across unseen real image domains. However, existing paradigms either suffer from limited segmentation performance when applied to abdominal organs, or require dataset-specific finetuning. To address these limitations, we propose ReSeg, a novel two-stage retraining-free framework for domain-agnostic zero-shot abdominal organ segmentation. At the first stage, our organ-agnostic synthetic data-driven pretraining approach exploits semantically and visually diverse synthetic images generated by a dedicated data engine to optimize a Generalizable Semantic Representation Network (GSRNet). The network is thereby capable of learning semantic features robust against variations in anatomical structure, imaging contrast, resolution and spatial context, which provide universal representation capabilities that serve as a foundation for segmentation learning. Subsequently, in the second stage, we continue to train an Organ-specific Encoder-decoder Segmentation Network (OESNet), whose encoder is initialized with the pretrained weights. This training process is facilitated by another dedicated data engine, which generates diversified visual images while strictly retaining the inherent spatial layout of abdominal organs. Comprehensive evaluation on seven abdominal organ segmentation datasets across three different modalities including CT, MRI, and PET demonstrates that ReSeg consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods while eliminating the need for real training images.

title: From Canon to Nikon: Camera Domain Shift and Potential Equity Implications in Retinal AI
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy is a leading cause of preventable blindness, yet access to regular screening remains limited worldwide. AI offers a scalable approach, but its performance can be sensitive to image quality and acquisition conditions. In a Brazilian cohort of 8,524 patients, retinal images acquired with the Nikon NF5050 were more than twice as likely to have inadequate image quality compared with those acquired with the Canon CR-2, despite refurbished Canon systems costing more than twice as much as Nikon systems. This potential cost-quality trade-off highlights an important consideration for the reliability of AI systems deployed across heterogeneous imaging systems. Using a frozen pretrained retinal foundation model, we systematically evaluate whether camera-associated performance differences persist across 12 retinal disease classification tasks, four input resolutions, and five downstream classifiers. We find that camera-associated performance differences vary substantially across tasks, and that neither higher input resolution nor classifier choice consistently mitigates cross-camera variation. These findings identify camera platform as a potentially overlooked source of performance variability, with implications for the safety and reliability of retinal AI when deployed across heterogeneous imaging systems. We release all source code, evaluation scripts, and per-task results on GitHub to support reproducible benchmarking.

title: Two for One: Privileged Learning for Resource-Constrained Screening
abstract: Machine learning systems are often developed under data-rich conditions but deployed when only incomplete information is available. A natural example arises in colour fundus photography (CFP), where both eyes are commonly imaged because they can provide complementary information for ocular disease assessment. Prior approaches that exploit bilateral information either fuse both eyes in a single model or use knowledge distillation to compress a dual-eye teacher into a lightweight student that still requires both images at test time. However, bilateral acquisition may not always be feasible. We thus propose a privileged learning framework in which a teacher model has access to bilateral CFP images during training and learns representations informed by information from both eyes, while the student is trained to transfer this knowledge from the bilateral teacher using only a single-eye image as input. At inference, the student operates exclusively on this single-eye input and does not require the contralateral image. Experimental results show consistent improvements in area under the receiver operating characteristic curve over conventional monocular training, with the largest gains observed for left-eye images for the detection of age-related macular degeneration (0.931 vs. 0.966) and diabetic retinopathy (0.789 vs. 0.836).%, while requiring only a single-eye image at inference. By enabling models to benefit from bilateral information during training while requiring only a single-eye image at inference, our approach may support more reliable deployment in resource-constrained clinical and screening environments.

title: DGCM-SSFA: Dual-Granularity Cross-Modulation and Sparse Strip Frequency Attention for Efficient 3T-to-7T MRI Synthesis
abstract: Synthesizing high-fidelity 7T MRI from routinely acquired 3T scans offers a practical pathway to enhanced neuroimaging without the prohibitive cost of ultra-high-field scanners. While existing deep learning approaches have achieved promising results, state-of-the-art methods typically rely on either large-scale architectures exceeding 45 million parameters or computationally intensive ensemble strategies, limiting their practicality in resource-constrained clinical environments. In this work, we propose a compact multi-domain attention framework, termed DGCM-SSFA, that achieves competitive synthesis quality with only 11M parameters. The proposed architecture integrates two complementary modules into a U-Net Transformer backbone. First, a Dual-Granularity Cross-Modulated Feature Modulator (DGCM) is embedded at multiple hierarchical levels to enhance local edge and texture details through Sobel-guided spatial attention and depthwise frequency-aware channel attention with cross-branch gating. Second, a Sparse Strip Frequency Attention (SSFA) module at the bottleneck captures global spatial context via strip-pooled attention with near-linear complexity, while simultaneously performing FFT-based spectral modulation in the frequency domain. These two modules operate synergistically with the backbone's native channel attention, forming a triple-granularity feature refinement pipeline. Extensive experiments on the UNC and BNU 3T-to-7T MRI datasets across T1w and T2w modalities demonstrate that DGCM-SSFA achieves strong structural fidelity, attaining an SSIM of 0.8431 on BNU T2w---approaching the best benchmark value of 0.8624---and 0.8100 on BNU T1w, while using substantially fewer parameters than Transformer-based alternatives such as ResViT (123.4M) and FS-RWKV (45.4M).

title: Estimating Performance for Safe Deployment of Machine Learning Models
abstract: The main challenge in applying deep neural networks to real-world scenarios lies in distributional discrepancies between training and test datasets, often caused by variations in data acquisition conditions. Assessing the performance of pre-trained models without labels is crucial for safety, but this is complicated by deep models' overly optimistic probabilistic outputs, often exacerbated by class imbalances, leading to unreliable predictions. To address these issues, we introduce MOVAL, a novel MOdel eVALuation tool that estimates performance using unlabeled test data. MOVAL incorporates class-wise confidence calibration to adjust model outputs, allowing for the estimation of metrics beyond accuracy and mitigating the detrimental effects of class imbalance on confidence calibration. Additionally, we propose an ensemble approach that combines multiple calibrated confidence scores for a more robust solution. We validate MOVAL on natural and medical image datasets with various acquisition shifts, covering tasks from classification to segmentation. It achieves state-of-the-art results across evaluation metrics such as accuracy, F1-Score, AUC, and more. Furthermore, we demonstrate that MOVAL provides accurate performance estimations at the class, instance, and pixel levels, ensuring the transparent and safe deployment of machine learning models. We provide MOVAL as a deployment tool for monitoring and estimating performance under a range of domain shifts.

title: OpenMAP-HIE: Pathology Informed Score-based Diffusion Model for Unsupervised Neonatal Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy Lesion Segmentation
abstract: Accurate localization of neonatal hypoxic--ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) lesions on apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) images is clinically important but is limited by scarce expert annotations and substantial variation in lesion appearance. We propose OpenMAP-HIE, a pathology-informed score-based diffusion model for unsupervised HIE lesion localization without voxel-wise lesion supervision. A denoising diffusion model learns the healthy neonatal ADC distribution, while a ControlNet-based conditional branch preserves patient-specific anatomy. At inference, anomaly evidence is derived directly from differences between conditional and unconditioned noise predictions at independently evaluated diffusion noise levels, avoiding dependence on a final pseudo-healthy reconstruction or sequential reverse-diffusion chain. Based on the characteristic ADC reduction associated with acute HIE, only discrepancies consistent with the expected pathological direction are retained and aggregated across noise levels using a geometric mean. Spatial mean filtering further suppresses isolated responses. The framework was evaluated on the BONBID-HIE dataset. The ADC-only method achieved a Dice score of $0.283\pm0.244$, average precision of $0.505$, Hausdorff distance of $25.45\pm15.63$ mm, mean average surface distance of $9.40\pm8.49$ mm, and normalized surface distance of $0.355\pm0.236$, providing the best overlap and surface-distance performance among the evaluated unsupervised methods and Dice performance comparable to supervised ADC-only models. Optional population-derived ADC $Z$-map refinement further increased Dice to $0.602\pm0.269$. These findings support pathology-informed score discrepancies as a useful signal for neonatal HIE lesion localization, while highlighting remaining challenges in detecting small and low-contrast lesions.

title: Reading the Mask: Descriptor-Grounded BI-RADS Rationale Generation for Breast MRI Segmentation
abstract: Deep learning based models accurately delineate tumours on dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI (DCE-MRI), but segmentation masks alone do not provide the rationales or reasoning used by radiologists to assess the lesion suspicion. This limits the explainability as well the clinical integration. We investigate whether clinically relevant descriptors can instead be derived from the segmentation masks and their dynamic contrast-enhancement series. We have used Breast Imaging Reporting and Data System (BI-RADS) guidelines as a structured framework. Using these guidelines we designed a BI-RADS decision tree with eight quantitative measurements using radiomics, together with the lesion size and component count, that determine the descriptors at eight nodes. Using these descriptors we generate natural-language rationale using a large language model. The model was constrained to express only the derived records from the decision tree. After applying this framework to the expert and automatic masks of each of the 1,506 cases in the MAMA-MIA dataset, we generated a reproducible corpus of 3,012 BI-RADS grounded rationales. We obtained a faithfulness score of 99.98% and a counterfactual accuracy of 99.3%, indicating that the generated rationales faithfully verbalises the measured descriptors and correctly reflects changes in the underlying record. Agreement between the descriptors from expert and automatic masks falls from 0.832 to 0.549 as mask quality falls from Good to Missed. The generated rationales are intended as draft representations for radiologist review and final sign-off rather than autonomous clinical reports.

title: An interpretable deep learning method for early hepatocellular carcinoma diagnosis on multiphase CT
abstract: Early diagnosis of hepatocellular carcinoma is critical to preserve access to curative treatment options. The Liver Imaging Reporting and Data System (LI-RADS) provides a standardized framework for non-invasive diagnosis on multiphase computed tomography, based on major visual imaging features. However, these features may be difficult to assess consistently, particularly in small liver lesions. We developed dLI-RADS, an interpretable artificial intelligence method designed to estimate the probability of hepatocellular carcinoma from multiphase computed tomography images of manually segmented liver lesions, while remaining aligned with LI-RADS-related imaging concepts. dLI-RADS combines neural network-derived predictions with handcrafted quantitative imaging measurements reflecting LI-RADS major features and integrates these inputs using logistic regression. In this multicenter retrospective study, patients with multiphase computed tomography and at least one liver lesion were included, while lesions larger than 40 mm were excluded. Histology served as the reference standard for hepatocellular carcinoma, and a composite reference standard was used for non-hepatocellular carcinoma lesions. The lesion-level accuracy of dLI-RADS and LI-RADS were compared on the internal evaluation set using 10,000-repetition bootstrap non-inferiority tests, with 5% margins and significance levels. On the external test set, sensitivities were similarly compared. dLI-RADS was non-inferior to LI-RADS for lesion-level accuracy in the internal evaluation set, achieving 80% accuracy compared with 74% for LI-RADS (p = 0.04)...

However, these features may be difficult to assess consistently, particularly in small liver lesions. We developed dLI-RADS, an interpretable artificial intelligence method designed to estimate the probability of hepatocellular carcinoma from multiphase computed tomography images of manually segmented liver lesions, while remaining aligned with LI-RADS-related imaging concepts. dLI-RADS combines neural network-derived predictions with handcrafted quantitative imaging measurements reflecting LI-RADS major features and integrates these inputs using logistic regression. In this multicenter retrospective study, patients with multiphase computed tomography and at least one liver lesion were included, while lesions larger than 40 mm were excluded. Histology served as the reference standard for hepatocellular carcinoma, and a composite reference standard was used for non-hepatocellular carcinoma lesions. The lesion-level accuracy of dLI-RADS and LI-RADS were compared on the internal evaluation set using 10,000-repetition bootstrap non-inferiority tests, with 5% margins and significance levels. On the external test set, sensitivities were similarly compared. dLI-RADS was non-inferior to LI-RADS for lesion-level accuracy in the internal evaluation set, achieving 80% accuracy compared with 74% for LI-RADS (p = 0.04)...

title: Reference Manual of MEDiml
abstract: Radiomics is the high-throughput extraction of quantitative features (e.g., tumor shape, intensity distributions, and texture) from medical images to characterize tissues and uncover disease patterns invisible to the human eye. These features can serve as candidate imaging biomarkers for cancer diagnosis, prognosis, and classification. However, extracting thousands of features makes it difficult to identify the most informative ones for a given clinical task, while implementing an end-to-end workflow can require programming expertise that limits accessibility for clinical researchers. Hence, we propose MEDiml, an open-source, standards-compliant radiomics platform connecting feature extraction, predictive modeling, and interpretation through complementary graphical and programmatic interfaces. MEDiml combines a Python package (MEDiml-pkg) with a graphical desktop application (MEDiml-app) that enables researchers to conduct experiments without writing code. Both interfaces use the same computational implementation, and code generation exports graphically configured workflows as executable Python code, facilitating reproducibility and collaboration between clinical researchers and computational scientists. A typical MEDiml workflow includes image preprocessing, radiomic feature extraction, feature set reduction, model training and evaluation, and interpretation using feature importance. Feature sets can be grouped into levels of radiomic complexity (morphological, intensity-based, textural, and filter-based) to evaluate whether more complex features provide additional predictive value. This reference manual documents the radiomics concepts, workflow, software components, architecture, and installation, compares MEDiml with existing tools, and demonstrates its complexity-driven workflow on five oncological imaging cohorts comprising 2,104 patients. Resources: www.mediml.app.

title: Learning to Measure and Diagnose: A Clinical-Dictionary Radiomic Bottleneck Model for Thyroid Nodule Classification
abstract: Thyroid ultrasound supports the assessment of nodule malignancy, but classification predictions often lack evidence linked to familiar clinical descriptions. Radiomics provides explicitly defined measurements that can support such explanations through a clinical dictionary. However, using these measurements as interpretable evidence requires reliable estimation from ultrasound images and preservation of measurement fidelity when optimizing classification performance. We propose a clinical-dictionary radiomic bottleneck model for thyroid nodule classification. Within this model, Family-Aware Radiomic Learning (FARL) estimates measurements with balanced supervision across feature families. Fidelity-Guided Bottleneck Modeling (FGBM) constructs a fixed bottleneck, followed by joint optimization of measurement estimation and classification under fidelity guidance. Decision evidence decomposition then traces feature contributions through a linear classifier and organizes them by clinical dictionary categories. Experiments on ThyroidXL and TN3K show competitive classification performance, while case studies illustrate feature contributions for benign and malignant nodules. These findings indicate interpretable classification with inspectable quantitative evidence informed by clinical knowledge. Code is available online.

title: Controlling Variability in~Neuroimaging Analysis Pipelines with~Software Product Lines
abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is an acquisition technique used for medical diagnosis. It is notably used for structural and functional MRI (or fMRI) image analysis. MRI data is known to be complex and noisy, so pipelines are created to extract and enhance relevant information in retrieved images. The NARPS study highlighted the significant variability that can emerge from different pipelines set up by independent teams while trying to answer the same research question about brain functioning. Having different implementations realizing the same task is a typical playground for software product lines (SPLs), which may be out of the sight of neuroimage practitioners. Thus, proposing an SPL out of these different pipelines falls back on a typical reverse-engineering problem with its usual difficulties. In this document, we advocate for the conceptual adoption of SPL principles as a promising direction to improve reproducibility and consistency in neuroimaging research.

title: Expandable Modality Experts for Medical Vision-Language Learning
abstract: Learning across medical imaging modalities requires making use of images without paired text and accommodating new domains while retaining existing representations. We propose a medical vision-language technique built around an expandable bank of modality experts. Its Multiway Transformer combines shared visual computation with deterministically routed feed-forward experts and a separate text pathway. A modality-aware visual tokenizer supplies targets for masked pretraining on 19.4 million unpaired image rows across seven modalities; contrastive alignment then uses 3.23 million image-text pairs. Additional fundus and optical coherence tomography experts learn from paired data while the original image and text embedding paths remain frozen. With a ViT-Large backbone, the proposed technique achieves the best or tied-best result in 24 of 25 benchmark settings across nine modalities: 10 of 11 zero-shot classification benchmarks, all 10 linear probes, and all four retrieval benchmarks. Mean balanced accuracy is 0.674 for zero-shot classification and 0.856 for linear probing, and mean bidirectional retrieval recall is 20.70%. A separate three-seed sequential experiment with matched adaptation data yields fundus and OCT retrieval gains of 14.95 and 9.31 percentage points, with no measured loss on preceding fundus or pathology tasks. The preservation argument requires unchanged existing computation paths and inference conditions, and feature-identity checks verify retention on evaluated inputs. The proposed technique provides a modular approach to learning and expanding medical vision-language representations.

title: ViBMR: A Large-Scale Multi-Sequence Brain MRI Dataset and Comprehensive Evaluation for Vietnamese Radiology Report Generation
abstract: Automated radiology report generation for multi-sequence brain MRI holds strong promise for alleviating radiologists' workload, yet it remains a demanding problem: brain MRI studies are inherently volumetric, each pulse sequence carries complementary diagnostic information, and annotated data are critically scarce for low-resource clinical languages. Existing brain MRI-report resources are still dominated by English reports, translated clinical text, or datasets adapted from task-specific imaging benchmarks, leaving routine low-resource clinical reporting and heterogeneous multi-sequence MRI protocols insufficiently represented. To bridge this gap, we introduce ViBMR, to the best of our knowledge, the first large-scale multi-sequence brain MRI dataset paired with routine Vietnamese clinical reports, comprising 3,649 patients and 11,875 MRI series across T1, T2, FLAIR, and contrast-enhanced T1 sequences. Building on ViBMR, we establish a comprehensive evaluation setup for brain MRI report generation, covering representative medical vision-language models, multi-sequence inputs, and feature aggregation strategies. The results provide key insights into dataset characteristics and model behavior, while demonstrating the necessity of native low-resource clinical datasets for reliable Vietnamese-origin brain MRI report generation. Our dataset and baseline models will be released for non-commercial research.

title: A Contrastive Learning Framework for Label-Efficient Gastric Cancer Detection and Intra-Tumour Progression Analysis
abstract: Gastric Cancer is among the leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide. The complexity and variability of histopathological images pose significant challenges for both pathologists and computer-based diagnostics, creating a growing need for machine learning approaches capable of capturing meaningful representations from limited labelled data. Selfsupervised Contrastive Learning (CL) has demonstrated promising results in natural image analysis; however, its application to gastric cancer histopathology remains underexplored. This paper proposes an integrated CL framework built on a ResNet50 encoder trained under the NT-Xent objective, without reliance on ImageNet pre-training, to learn discriminative and staining-invariant representations from H&E-stained tissue patches. The learned embeddings are transferred to a supervised downstream classifier for binary tumour/normal (TUM/NOR) detection, achieving a test accuracy of 83.13%, an AUC-ROC of 0.9087, and an Average Precision of 0.9063 - competitive with recent supervised and weakly-supervised approaches on comparable histopathology benchmarks. Beyond binary diagnosis, the framework applies K-Means clustering to tumour embeddings to identify four geometrically separable pseudo-stage clusters, confirmed by a Random Forest classifier achieving 97% accuracy and a mean Dice coefficient of 0.97, demonstrating the capacity of CL representations to encode progression-relevant morphological variation without stage-level annotations. Grad-CAM explainability is integrated throughout to ensure model transparency. The complete system is deployed via a Streamlit clinical interface. Compared to recent state-of-the-art methods the proposed framework operates with substantially fewer labelled samples while additionally providing unsupervised progression stratification and interpretable outputs, addressing a gap not covered by existing approaches.

title: Multimodal Machine Learning-Based Prediction of Relapse in Major Depressive Disorder.
abstract: Importance Early identification of patients at high risk of relapse is key to personalized preventive strategies in major depressive disorder (MDD). However, current predictive models do not adequately account for the multimodal factors contributing to MDD relapse and fail to provide clinically meaningful predictions. Objective To predict relapse within 2 years in patients with MDD by using a comprehensive machine learning pipeline that integrates an unprecedented set of multimodal data. Design, setting, and participants This naturalistic longitudinal prognostic study used data from the Marburg-Münster Affective Disorders Cohort Study, with baseline assessments collected from October 2014 to May 2019 and follow-up approximately 2 years later, between October 2016 and June 2021. Data analysis was conducted between July 2024 and June 2026. The study was performed at 2 sites in Germany (Marburg and Münster), with participants recruited from psychiatric inpatient and outpatient departments and the general population. Patients meeting diagnostic criteria for current or lifetime MDD without history of neurological or severe somatic conditions were included. Exposure Natural course of illness in patients with MDD. Main outcomes and measures Balanced accuracy (BACC) for binary prediction of relapse vs no relapse during 2-year follow-up served as the primary outcome. Baseline features comprised 9 modalities including clinical and psychometric data, 4 structural and functional magnetic resonance imaging modalities, genetics, neurocognition, blood markers, and gut microbiome. Results A total of 564 patients with a current or lifetime MDD diagnosis were included (367 female [65.1%]; mean [SD] age, 37.34 [13.38] years). A total of 270 patients relapsed during the 2-year follow-up, while 294 did not. Mean (SD) BACC for the prediction of relapse ranged from 47.21% (5.85%) to 64.43% (6.63%). The best-performing model was solely based on few clinical relapse risk factors, while multimodal data integration did not improve performance. Conclusions and relevance In this prognostic study, the models achieved moderate accuracy, yet the results suggest limited scope for guiding individual-level clinical decision-making. Predictive performance was largely driven by established clinical risk factors, indicating limited incremental value of multimodal measures when assessed at a single time point. Future advances may instead benefit from dynamic modeling approaches that more closely align temporally evolving multimodal markers with longitudinal clinical outcomes.
originalAbstract:
Importance

Early identification of patients at high risk of relapse is key to personalized preventive strategies in major depressive disorder (MDD). However, current predictive models do not adequately account for the multimodal factors contributing to MDD relapse and fail to provide clinically meaningful predictions.

Objective

To predict relapse within 2 years in patients with MDD by using a comprehensive machine learning pipeline that integrates an unprecedented set of multimodal data.

Design, setting, and participants

This naturalistic longitudinal prognostic study used data from the Marburg-Münster Affective Disorders Cohort Study, with baseline assessments collected from October 2014 to May 2019 and follow-up approximately 2 years later, between October 2016 and June 2021. Data analysis was conducted between July 2024 and June 2026. The study was performed at 2 sites in Germany (Marburg and Münster), with participants recruited from psychiatric inpatient and outpatient departments and the general population. Patients meeting diagnostic criteria for current or lifetime MDD without history of neurological or severe somatic conditions were included.

Exposure

Natural course of illness in patients with MDD.

Main outcomes and measures

Balanced accuracy (BACC) for binary prediction of relapse vs no relapse during 2-year follow-up served as the primary outcome. Baseline features comprised 9 modalities including clinical and psychometric data, 4 structural and functional magnetic resonance imaging modalities, genetics, neurocognition, blood markers, and gut microbiome.

Results

A total of 564 patients with a current or lifetime MDD diagnosis were included (367 female [65.1%]; mean [SD] age, 37.34 [13.38] years). A total of 270 patients relapsed during the 2-year follow-up, while 294 did not. Mean (SD) BACC for the prediction of relapse ranged from 47.21% (5.85%) to 64.43% (6.63%). The best-performing model was solely based on few clinical relapse risk factors, while multimodal data integration did not improve performance.

Conclusions and relevance

In this prognostic study, the models achieved moderate accuracy, yet the results suggest limited scope for guiding individual-level clinical decision-making. Predictive performance was largely driven by established clinical risk factors, indicating limited incremental value of multimodal measures when assessed at a single time point. Future advances may instead benefit from dynamic modeling approaches that more closely align temporally evolving multimodal markers with longitudinal clinical outcomes.

title: A Recurrent 3'UTR Variant in CAPN3 Highlights the Diagnostic Impact of Non-Coding Variants in Limb-Girdle Muscular Dystrophies.
abstract: Objective A substantial proportion of individuals with suspected genetic conditions, including neuromuscular disorders, lack a definitive molecular diagnosis. Non-coding variants, particularly those in the 3' untranslated region (3´UTR), which regulate mRNA stability, translation, and localization, may underlie part of this gap. We investigated the clinical, genetic, and functional relevance of a novel 3'UTR variant in CAPN3 in individuals with persistent hyperCKemia, most of whom also presented with proximal muscle weakness. Methods Clinical assessment, including muscle biopsy and muscle magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), was performed in individuals harboring the CAPN3 c.*534T>C variant. In silico analyses included the assessment of miRNA binding, mRNA secondary structure, creation or disruption of a poly-A tail, and RNA-binding protein (RBP) motifs. A luciferase reporter assay with the c.*534T>C and reference sequence, in the presence or absence of RBFOX1 co-expression, was performed. Results We identified 13 individuals from 11 unrelated families presenting with persistent hyperCKemia, commonly accompanied by proximal muscle weakness and myalgia, all harboring the c.*534T>C variant in combination with a previously identified heterozygous CAPN3 variant. Western blot analyses consistently demonstrated absent or markedly reduced calpain-3 expression, and muscle RNA sequencing (RNAseq) showed reduced CAPN3 levels. In silico analyses indicated that the c.*534T>C variant creates a novel binding site for the RNA-binding protein RBFOX1. Luciferase reporter assays supported a regulatory effect of the identified variant on calpain-3 expression. Interpretation Our results show that a recurrent non-coding CAPN3 variant causes disease by disrupting post-transcriptional regulation and demonstrate a generalizable principle, as 3'UTR variants can affect mRNA stability and protein expression across neuromuscular and other Mendelian diseases. Although often difficult to interpret as pathogenic, these variants can be therapeutically actionable, highlighting the importance of systematically investigating non-coding regions in unsolved genetic cases. ANN NEUROL 2026.

title: PRISM, a Bidirectional NMR Foundation Model: From Peak List to Structure and Back.
abstract: Determining molecular structures from nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectra is a central challenge in organic chemistry, natural-product discovery, and drug development. Established computational approaches are robust within their design scope, but direct spectra-to-structure models have relied largely on simulated spectra or narrow chemical subsets, limiting robustness on real data. We introduce PRISM (Peak-Resolved Integrative Spectral Model), a unified transformer encoder-decoder bridging experimental spectra and molecular structures bidirectionally: spec2mol translates 1 H and 13 C peak lists into SMILES strings, while mol2spec predicts full spectra from SMILES. Spec2mol integrates six chemistry-aware modules that embed domain knowledge into learning. Trained on 1.19 million experimental NMR-structure pairs spanning 49 atom types, spec2mol achieves 60.1% stereo-aware (72.5% stereo-unaware) top-1 exact match accuracy, 16.7 percentage points above the strongest published deep learning (DL) models under identical conditions on the same test set. Mol2spec attains 1 H MAE of 0.036 ppm and 13 C MAE of 0.358 ppm in under 0.3 s per molecule. Fine-tuned on photochemical reactions, spec2mol achieved 69.2% (85.2%) top-1 accuracy on real spectra. Together, PRISM is a practical decision-support system that proposes and ranks candidate structures for expert verification, and a fast forward predictor for reaction analysis and virtual screening. PRISM is freely available at https://prism.uni-muenster.de/.

title: Artificial intelligence applications in intracranial electroencephalography for epilepsy management: Insights from AI in Epilepsy 2025.
abstract: Intracranial electroencephalography (iEEG) provides direct recordings of cortical activity and remains central to the presurgical evaluation of drug-resistant focal epilepsy. However, the high dimensionality and complexity of iEEG data increasingly challenge conventional visual interpretation. Artificial intelligence (AI) methods have accelerated quantitative analyses in electrophysiology, supporting localization, outcome prediction, and therapeutic decision-making in epilepsy. This article reviews recent advances in the application of AI to iEEG in epilepsy and in particular stereo-EEG, although the concepts discussed are broadly relevant across iEEG modalities. Although many of these approaches have shown encouraging results, the current evidence remains largely preliminary, with most studies being retrospective, single-center investigations that lack independent external validation. AI-based integration of iEEG with multimodal magnetic resonance imaging shows promise for improving surgical planning in drug-resistant focal epilepsy. Concurrently, early studies suggest that AI-driven iEEG analysis may enhance epileptogenic zone identification by detecting subtle electrophysiological signatures, network interactions, and temporal dynamics. These multimodal frameworks emphasize distributed epileptic networks rather than isolated focal abnormalities. AI is also reshaping how iEEG-guided stimulation is designed and interpreted. Data-driven approaches have the potential to optimize stimulation parameters, predict network responses, and clarify mechanisms underlying diagnostic and therapeutic stimulation, laying the groundwork for adaptive, patient-specific neuromodulation. Beyond short-term epilepsy monitoring, AI applications increasingly incorporate continuous sensing, longitudinal network modeling, and integration with implantable neurotechnology platforms. Although these developments require prospective multicenter studies with external validation before widespread clinical implementation, advances in multimodal data integration, interpretable modeling, and continuous sensing position AI-enhanced iEEG as an emerging platform for precision brain network medicine for epilepsy.

title: A Pain in the Buttocks: Practice Article for Sonographically Imaging the Quadratus Femoris and Ischiofemoral Impingement.
abstract: Ischiofemoral impingement (IFI) results in buttock, hip, and groin pain which can radiate down the leg. Clinical diagnosis of IFI is challenging due to the overlap of other syndrome symptoms, which can delay appropriate management. Hip external rotation reduces the ischiofemoral and quadratus femoris (QF) spaces, compressing the QF muscle between the ischial tuberosity and the lesser trochanter. Ultrasound imaging can demonstrate dynamic entrapment of the QF, including assessment of symptom provocation and concurrently identify injury or irritation of nearby structures including the peri-QF fat, sciatic nerve, and proximal hamstring tendons.

title: Multimodal Ultrasound for Early Prognostic Assessment During Definitive Radiotherapy in Locally Advanced Cervical Cancer.
abstract: Purpose To investigate the prognostic value of early multimodal ultrasound parameters in patients with locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC) undergoing definitive radiotherapy. Methods This retrospective exploratory study included 31 patients with histologically confirmed cervical squamous cell carcinoma who underwent definitive radiotherapy with or without concurrent chemotherapy. Grayscale ultrasound and shear wave elastography (SWE) were performed in all patients at baseline and approximately 2 weeks after radiotherapy initiation, whereas complete contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) data were available for 22 patients. Unfavorable outcomes were defined as progression, recurrence, or death during follow-up after radiotherapy initiation. ROC analysis was performed to evaluate individual parameters, and a logistic regression model incorporating baseline SWE mean and tumor maximum diameter at the two-week assessment was internally validated using 1000 bootstrap resamples to estimate optimism-corrected performance. Exploratory time-dependent ROC analyses were performed using progression-free survival data to assess model discrimination at different follow-up time points. Results Patients with unfavorable outcomes showed higher baseline SWE mean values (153 vs. 106.5 kPa, p = 0.039) and larger residual tumor maximum diameters 2 weeks after radiotherapy initiation (36 vs. 32 mm, p = 0.045). The combined model showed an apparent AUC of 0.775 and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.735. Exploratory time-dependent ROC analysis yielded AUC values of 0.855, 0.840, and 0.719 at 12, 24, and 36 months, respectively. Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated shorter progression-free survival in the higher-risk group than in the lower-risk group according to the combined model (log-rank p = 0.022). In exploratory CEUS subgroup analysis, a greater reduction in time to peak was associated with unfavorable outcomes (p = 0.039). Conclusions Baseline tumor stiffness and early residual tumor size assessed by multimodal ultrasound may offer complementary prognostic information for exploratory risk stratification in patients with LACC undergoing definitive radiotherapy. Further prospective validation is warranted.

title: Quantitative UTE MRI Differences in the Meniscus Following ACL Reconstruction: A Prospective Cohort Study Using 3D Ultrashort Echo Time Adiabatic T1rho and Magnetization Transfer Imaging.
abstract: Background ACLR is associated with altered joint loading and increased risk of post-traumatic osteoarthritis. Conventional MRI has limited sensitivity to early meniscal differences because of short-T2 signal decay and magic-angle effects. Purpose To evaluate whether 3D ultrashort echo time imaging-based adiabatic T1rho (UTE-Adiab-T1rho) and ultrashort echo time imaging-based macromolecular fraction (UTE-MMF) identify regional quantitative MRI differences after ACLR. Study type Prospective longitudinal cohort study. Population 30 control scans, 19 ACLR scans at 6-12 months, and 13 ACLR scans at 12+ months were analyzed. Mean ages were 34.5, 34.5, and 37.2 years; female/male counts were 15/15, 9/10, and 8/5. Field strength/sequence Participants underwent 3-T knee MRI with 3D fat-saturated UTE-Adiab-T1rho and UTE magnetization transfer sequences. Assessment UTE-Adiab-T1rho and UTE-MMF maps were generated with single-component exponential and two-pool magnetization transfer models. Values were extracted from four meniscal regions of interest by a blinded reader, with blinded redelineation in a subset. Patient-reported outcomes included International Knee Documentation Committee, Knee Injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score, and Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index scores. Statistical tests Linear mixed-effects models accounted for repeated observations. Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction was applied. Results UTE-Adiab-T1rho showed significant group (q = 0.001) and region (q < 0.001) effects. Compared with controls, UTE-Adiab-T1rho was higher in LAM at 6-12 months (+5.60 ms; q = 0.035) and 12+ months (+7.09 ms; q = 0.028), and in LPM at 12+ months (+6.35 ms; q = 0.035). UTE-MMF showed significant group (q = 0.041) and region (q < 0.001) effects. LPM UTE-MMF was lower than controls at 6-12 months (-3.56 percentage points; q = 0.028) and 12+ months (-3.10 percentage points; q = 0.049). No 6-12 versus 12+ month MRI or PROM contrast survived FDR correction. MRI-PROM associations were not FDR-significant (all q ≥ 0.383). Data conclusion UTE-Adiab-T1rho and UTE-MMF mapping identified regional MRI differences after ACLR. Pairwise differences were concentrated in lateral regions, but corrected group-by-region interactions were not significant. PROMs were worse after ACLR but did not differ between postoperative windows after correction. Evidence level 2. Technical efficacy stage 2.

Background

ACLR is associated with altered joint loading and increased risk of post-traumatic osteoarthritis. Conventional MRI has limited sensitivity to early meniscal differences because of short-T2 signal decay and magic-angle effects.

Purpose

To evaluate whether 3D ultrashort echo time imaging-based adiabatic T1rho (UTE-Adiab-T1rho) and ultrashort echo time imaging-based macromolecular fraction (UTE-MMF) identify regional quantitative MRI differences after ACLR.

Study type

Prospective longitudinal cohort study.

Population

30 control scans, 19 ACLR scans at 6-12 months, and 13 ACLR scans at 12+ months were analyzed. Mean ages were 34.5, 34.5, and 37.2 years; female/male counts were 15/15, 9/10, and 8/5.

Field strength/sequence

Participants underwent 3-T knee MRI with 3D fat-saturated UTE-Adiab-T1rho and UTE magnetization transfer sequences.

Assessment

UTE-Adiab-T1rho and UTE-MMF maps were generated with single-component exponential and two-pool magnetization transfer models. Values were extracted from four meniscal regions of interest by a blinded reader, with blinded redelineation in a subset. Patient-reported outcomes included International Knee Documentation Committee, Knee Injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score, and Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index scores.

Statistical tests

Linear mixed-effects models accounted for repeated observations. Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction was applied.

Results

UTE-Adiab-T1rho showed significant group (q = 0.001) and region (q < 0.001) effects. Compared with controls, UTE-Adiab-T1rho was higher in LAM at 6-12 months (+5.60 ms; q = 0.035) and 12+ months (+7.09 ms; q = 0.028), and in LPM at 12+ months (+6.35 ms; q = 0.035). UTE-MMF showed significant group (q = 0.041) and region (q < 0.001) effects. LPM UTE-MMF was lower than controls at 6-12 months (-3.56 percentage points; q = 0.028) and 12+ months (-3.10 percentage points; q = 0.049). No 6-12 versus 12+ month MRI or PROM contrast survived FDR correction. MRI-PROM associations were not FDR-significant (all q ≥ 0.383).

Data conclusion

UTE-Adiab-T1rho and UTE-MMF mapping identified regional MRI differences after ACLR. Pairwise differences were concentrated in lateral regions, but corrected group-by-region interactions were not significant. PROMs were worse after ACLR but did not differ between postoperative windows after correction.

Evidence level

2.

Technical efficacy stage

title: Value of Multimodal Ultrasound Imaging With Super-Resolution in the Differential Diagnosis of Benign and Malignant Superficial Lymph Nodes: A Dual-Center Prospective Study.
abstract: Objectives Accurate differential diagnosis of benign and malignant superficial lymph nodes (LNs) is critical for clinical management. The objectives of this study were to explore the feasibility and clinical value of super-resolution ultrasound (SRUS) in the differential diagnosis of superficial lymphadenopathy and to establish and validate a multimodal ultrasound diagnostic model based on conventional ultrasound (US), contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS), and SRUS, so as to improve the accuracy of distinguishing benign from malignant superficial LNs in clinical practice. Methods A total of 200 LNs from 165 patients with superficial lymphadenectasis were prospectively enrolled from two medical centers. All patients underwent conventional US, CEUS, and SRUS imaging. Predictive models were constructed based on the conventional US, CEUS, and SRUS features in the training cohort, and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity, and specificity were calculated to evaluate their predictive performance in the external validation cohort. Results The training cohort comprised 117 patients with a total of 140 LNs including 46 benign and 94 malignant lesions. The validation cohort included 48 patients with 60 LNs in total, with 21 benign and 39 malignant lesions. Among the models constructed based on the training cohort, the SRUS model exhibited significantly superior diagnostic performance (AUC = 0.822) to the conventional US and CEUS models (P < .05). The combined model, integrating all three modalities, achieved an AUC of 0.892 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.833-0.952) in the training cohort and 0.890 (95% CI: 0.791-0.990) in the external validation cohort, demonstrating excellent and stable diagnostic performance. Conclusion SRUS provides crucial imaging evidence for the non-invasive qualitative evaluation of LNs. The multimodal diagnostic model incorporating the features of US, CEUS, and SRUS can significantly improve the accuracy of distinguishing benign from malignant LNs.

title: Intraoperative Bone Marrow Frozen Sections Reduce Positive Final Margins in Mandibulectomy.
abstract: Objectives To assess the impact of intraoperative bone marrow frozen section (IBMFS) use on final margin status and survival outcomes in patients undergoing mandibulectomy for squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) and non-SCC neoplasms. Methods A single-center retrospective cohort study was performed of patients undergoing segmental or marginal mandibulectomy for benign or malignant neoplasms between 2009 and 2025. The medical record was reviewed for demographic data, histopathologic disease features, treatment, and outcomes. Univariable and multivariable Cox regression analyses were used to evaluate associations between IBMFS and recurrence-free and overall survival among patients with SCC. Results Of 235 cases, IBMFS were performed in 80.4%. IBMFS analysis was associated with reduced rates of positive final bone margins (1.1% vs. 8.7%, p = 0.014) and overall positive margins (7.9% vs. 19.6%, p = 0.029). Positive IBMFS rate was higher among non-SCC neoplasms than SCC (23.5% vs. 3.5%, p = 0.007), with no significant difference in rate of final positive margins. IBMFS results demonstrated 90.0% sensitivity, 99.4% specificity, and 98.9% concordance with final histopathology. Among SCC patients, IBMFS use was not significantly associated with recurrence-free survival (aHR 0.671, p = 0.320) or overall survival (aHR 0.967, p = 0.923); only nodal disease and age were significantly associated with survival. Conclusions In this retrospective single-center cohort, IBMFS use was associated with improved final margin control across tumor types, including non-SCC neoplasms. Although no survival benefit was demonstrated, its association with margin clearance suggests that IBMFS may be a useful intraoperative adjunct in mandibulectomy for head and neck neoplasms. Level of evidence: 3

title: MRI-Derived Muscle Fat Fraction Reflects Disease Severity and Functional Impairment in Charcot-Marie-Tooth Disease Type 1A.
abstract: Introduction/aims Progressive intramuscular fat infiltration is a hallmark of neuromuscular degeneration in Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 1A (CMT1A). Quantitative assessment of muscle fat fraction (FF) by Dixon magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides an objective biomarker of disease severity, but manual segmentation is laborious and variable. This study explored whether automated MRI-based FF quantification reflects disease severity and functional decline in CMT1A. Methods Sixty-nine genetically confirmed patients with CMT1A who underwent 3D multi-echo Dixon lower-leg MRI were retrospectively analyzed. A deep learning-based segmentation model delineated four muscle compartments (anterior, lateral, deep posterior, superficial posterior) and mean FFs were computed volumetrically. Correlations were tested between MRI-derived FFs and clinical outcomes, including the Charcot-Marie-Tooth Neuropathy Score (CMTNSv2), Functional Disability Scale (FDS), and time-, strength-, distance-, and repetition-based performance. Partial correlations were adjusted for age and body mass index. Results All compartmental and total FFs correlated positively with CMTNSv2 and FDS (r = 0.39-0.49, p < 0.05). FFs were positively associated with time-based and negatively with strength-, distance-, and repetition-based measures. FF Anterior showed moderate correlations with stair climb time (r = 0.68, p < 0.001) and 6-min walk distance (r = -0.66, p < 0.001), with similar magnitudes across compartments. Most associations remained significant after adjustment. The lateral compartment showed the highest FF (median 33.2%), consistent with the peroneal pattern of CMT1A. Discussion Automated MRI-based FF quantification provides a reproducible biomarker of disease burden in CMT1A, reflecting clinical severity and functional decline, and may serve as an imaging outcome measure in future studies.

Introduction/aims

Progressive intramuscular fat infiltration is a hallmark of neuromuscular degeneration in Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 1A (CMT1A). Quantitative assessment of muscle fat fraction (FF) by Dixon magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides an objective biomarker of disease severity, but manual segmentation is laborious and variable. This study explored whether automated MRI-based FF quantification reflects disease severity and functional decline in CMT1A.

Methods

Sixty-nine genetically confirmed patients with CMT1A who underwent 3D multi-echo Dixon lower-leg MRI were retrospectively analyzed. A deep learning-based segmentation model delineated four muscle compartments (anterior, lateral, deep posterior, superficial posterior) and mean FFs were computed volumetrically. Correlations were tested between MRI-derived FFs and clinical outcomes, including the Charcot-Marie-Tooth Neuropathy Score (CMTNSv2), Functional Disability Scale (FDS), and time-, strength-, distance-, and repetition-based performance. Partial correlations were adjusted for age and body mass index.

Results

All compartmental and total FFs correlated positively with CMTNSv2 and FDS (r = 0.39-0.49, p < 0.05). FFs were positively associated with time-based and negatively with strength-, distance-, and repetition-based measures. FF Anterior showed moderate correlations with stair climb time (r = 0.68, p < 0.001) and 6-min walk distance (r = -0.66, p < 0.001), with similar magnitudes across compartments. Most associations remained significant after adjustment. The lateral compartment showed the highest FF (median 33.2%), consistent with the peroneal pattern of CMT1A.

Discussion

Automated MRI-based FF quantification provides a reproducible biomarker of disease burden in CMT1A, reflecting clinical severity and functional decline, and may serve as an imaging outcome measure in future studies.

title: Regional growth patterns of fetal corpus callosum at 18-32 weeks' gestation assessed by three-dimensional transvaginal neurosonography.
abstract: Objectives To evaluate the normal development of the fetal corpus callosum (CC) between 18 and 32 weeks' gestation using three-dimensional (3D) transvaginal neurosonography and to assess the effect of volume contrast imaging (VCI) on the measurement of fetal CC biometry. Methods This study included two cohorts of women with a singleton pregnancy: a prospective cohort attending the research clinic at Prince of Wales Hospital in Hong Kong SAR, China, between April 2019 and February 2025, at which 3D fetal brain volumes were acquired prospectively, and a retrospective cohort attending CRIFM Prenatal Medical Clinic in Osaka, Japan, between December 2018 and March 2025, from which archived 3D fetal brain volume datasets were retrieved. In both cohorts, 3D fetal brain volume data of the CC were acquired using transvaginal neurosonography between 18 and 32 weeks' gestation using the same acquisition protocol. Inclusion criteria were appropriately grown fetuses at 18 + 0 to 32 + 6 weeks' gestation, without suspected structural or chromosomal defects. In the midsagittal plane, using 3D volume multiplanar imaging, the CC length and total area were obtained and regional thickness at the genu, body and splenium were measured following a modified Garel's method. Additionally, the areas of five vertical CC segments defined by arithmetic fractions of the CC length following Witelson's classification (anterior one-third, anterior midbody, posterior midbody, isthmus and splenium) were obtained. All fetal biometric measurements were performed using non-VCI and VCI modes. Measurements obtained using non-VCI and VCI modes were compared using the paired t-test. title: Preoperative prevalence and risk factors for thromboembolic events following tibial plateau fractures: a retrospective analysis of an underestimated risk.
abstract: Background Tibial plateau fractures (TPF) are complex intra-articular injuries carrying a high risk of deep vein thrombosis (DVT), muscular vein thrombosis (MVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE). Preoperative thrombosis is frequently clinically silent yet may cause serious complications, whereas its detection delays definitive surgery. This study assessed the prevalence and risk factors of preoperative venous thromboembolic events (VTE) in surgically treated TPF before and after implementation of routine duplex ultrasound screening. Methods In this retrospective single-centre study at a level 1 trauma centre, all adult patients surgically treated for traumatic TPF (AO 41B/C) between January 2015 and August 2025 were reviewed (547 patients, 554 fractures). Until August 2020 duplex ultrasound (DUS) was performed only on clinical suspicion; from August 2020 onward routine preoperative DUS was progressively implemented. VTE were confirmed by DUS or CT angiography. Prevalences are reported per fracture and patient characteristics per patient; regression analyses were performed at fracture level, except for the patient-related model. Results With DUS restricted to clinical suspicion (cohort A; 246 fractures), the detected prevalence of preoperative VTE was 3.7% (95% CI 1.9-6.8) and that of DVT 2.4% (1.1-5.2). Under routine screening (cohort B; 205 screened fractures) it was 20.0% (15.1-26.0) and 17.1% (12.5-22.8), respectively, 82.9% of DVT being distal. Given the different diagnostic strategies, this reflects the higher diagnostic yield of screening rather than a true increase in VTE. In cohort B, 28 of 41 VTE (68.3%) and 24 of 35 DVT (68.6%) were clinically silent. Two patients had in-hospital cardiac arrest from PE: one died from a DVT undetected before screening was introduced, the other had an asymptomatic DVT identified by screening. VTE was independently associated with pre-existing therapeutic anticoagulation (adjusted OR 2.96, 95% CI 1.10-7.98) and with the duration of external fixation (adjusted OR 1.11 per day, 1.02-1.20). High-grade closed soft-tissue injury (adjusted OR 2.41, 1.07-5.45), polytrauma (adjusted OR 2.24, 1.07-4.68) and initial external fixation (univariable OR 3.60, 1.76-7.35) were also associated with VTE, but none remained significant after accounting for fixation duration (adjusted OR 1.42, 0.52-3.89; 1.96, 0.76-5.05; 0.62, 0.12-3.27), i.e. risk was driven by time in the fixator rather than by external fixation as such. Conclusions Surgically treated TPF carry a substantial burden of preoperative VTE, and routine DUS reveals a high proportion of clinically silent thrombosis that would otherwise remain undetected. Severe closed soft-tissue injury, pre-existing therapeutic anticoagulation and, above all, the duration of external fixation may help to identify patients at increased risk. As two diagnostic rather than two treatment strategies were compared, the study cannot determine whether screening improves outcomes or reduces PE; prospective evaluation of structured screening and risk-adapted thromboprophylaxis is warranted.

title: [Hepatic postinterventional imaging : Modality selection, assessment of therapeutic response, recognition, and radiological management of typical complications].
abstract: Background Postprocedural imaging following hepatic interventions is essential for monitoring treatment success and detecting complications. Objective To provide an overview of imaging follow-up after hepatic interventions (transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt [TIPS], percutaneous transhepatic cholangiography and drainage [PTCD], transarterial chemoembolization [TACE], ablation, selective internal radiotherapy [SIRT]), focusing on the selection of imaging modalities, the assessment of treatment success, and the recognition and radiological management of complications. Materials and methods Narrative review based on the current literature of hepatic radiological interventions. Results The procedure determines the choice of imaging modality. Following TIPS, functional monitoring is primarily performed using duplex ultrasound. PTCD follow-up focuses on drainage placement and bleeding complications. Following TACE and ablation, immediate hypoperfusion of the lesions is to be expected, whereas a temporary increase in size and peripheral enhancement may occur. Following SIRT, a delayed onset of the treatment effect, as detectable by imaging morphology, is characteristic. Bleeding, abscess formation, fistulas, stent occlusions or malfunctions, and tumor recurrences can be treated further using interventional radiology. Conclusion Knowledge of typical postprocedural imaging findings, as well as common complications and options for radiological treatment of complications, is crucial.

title: CT Perfusion in the differential diagnosis of glioblastomas and primary central nervous system lymphomas.
abstract: Purpose To compare perfusion parameters of glioblastomas and primary central nervous system lymphomas (PCNSL) using CT perfusion (CTP) and to assess the diagnostic performance of this technique for their preoperative differential diagnosis. Methods This single-center retrospective study included CTP data from 122 patients (57 with PCNSL and 65 with glioblastoma) examined at our hospital between 2006 and 2026. All diagnoses were histologically verified; no patient received chemotherapy, corticosteroids or radiotherapy prior to CTP. Imaging was performed on a 64-slice Optima 660 scanner (GE Medical Systems) using a prolonged perfusion protocol. Absolute (CBF, CBV, MTT, PS) and normalized (nCBF, nCBV, nMTT, nPS) perfusion parameters were obtained. The Mann-Whitney U test, Spearman correlation and ROC analysis were applied for statistical comparison. Results Glioblastomas demonstrated significantly higher CBF and CBV and lower MTT and PS values than PCNSL; the same pattern was observed for the normalized parameters. PS (AUC = 0.93), nPS (AUC = 0.90), nCBF (AUC = 0.91), nCBV (AUC = 0.90), CBF (AUC = 0.88) and CBV (AUC = 0.88) showed the highest diagnostic performance, whereas MTT and nMTT were less informative (AUC = 0.69-0.72). Conclusion CTP is a highly informative non-invasive quantitative imaging tool for the preoperative differentiation of glioblastomas and PCNSL. The inclusion of normalized perfusion parameters improves reproducibility and supports use in routine clinical practice and multicenter studies. CTP can be recommended whenever conventional CT and MRI fail to reliably distinguish these tumors.

title: Clinical evaluation of deep learning-based acquisition and reconstruction techniques for accelerated 2D shoulder magnetic resonance imaging acceleration at 3 T.
abstract: Purpose GE has recently developed Sonic DL MRI acceleration technology. We wished to (1) quantify scanner time reduction compared to the AIR Recon DL already in clinical use at our institution and (2) preliminarily evaluate any change in diagnostic findings between these methods. Methods A total of 30 outpatients undergoing routine shoulder MRI for shoulder pain were recruited. Each underwent routine AIR Recon DL and Sonic DL exams containing the same sequences. Three subspecialized musculoskeletal radiologists assessed image quality, graded pathology, and reported diagnostic confidence in a blinded fashion. Differences in image quality and confidence were compared using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Results Sonic DL reduced nominal acquisition time 38.7% compared to AIR Recon DL (6 min 15 s versus 10 min 12 s). Artifact was considered slightly worse on the routine examination (3.20 versus 3.37, P = 0.039); there was no significant difference in image quality, sharpness, or signal-to-noise ratio between routine and Sonic DL accelerated exams (P 0.171-0.861). Inter-reader agreement was broadly similar between routine-routine and routine-Sonic DL comparisons (median agreement 0.867 and 0.839, respectively). Within-reader analysis identified subacromial/subdeltoid bursitis and supraspinatus tendon tears more frequently on the routine protocol than on Sonic DL (P 0.049 and P 0.006, respectively). Conclusion Sonic DL enabled a 38.7% reduction in nominal shoulder MRI acquisition time with broadly comparable image quality and inter-reader agreement in this pilot cohort. Diagnostic equivalence was not established; subacromial/subdeltoid bursitis and supraspinatus tears were potentially less conspicuous on Sonic DL. A larger powered validation study would be needed to fully evaluate diagnostic performance.

title: Morphological Patterns of Fibrous-Dominant Dorsocervical Humps and a Mesh Technique for the Diffuse Subtype.
abstract: Background Fibrous-dominant dorsocervical humps remain a challenging surgical condition because dense collagen structure limits the effectiveness of conventional liposuction and adjunctive energy-based techniques. Current surgical decision-making lacks an objective framework based on the internal structural organization of fibrosis. Objective To characterize CT-based morphological patterns of fibrous-dominant dorsocervical humps and to introduce a Mesh release technique specifically designed for the diffuse fibrous subtype. Methods Preoperative axial computed tomography (CT) images from 102 patients were reviewed to evaluate the internal morphology of fibrous tissue. Two distinct patterns were identified: a localized (mass-dominant) fibrous subtype and a diffuse (septal-dominant) fibrous subtype. Diffuse cases underwent three-dimensional CT reconstruction to further characterize the spatial architecture of fibrous septa. Accordingly, a minimally invasive Mesh release technique was developed to achieve multidirectional, cross-plane disruption of the diffuse fibrous network. Clinical outcomes were evaluated using a 4-point esthetic grading scale, and complications were recorded. Results Among 102 patients, 65 (63.7%) demonstrated the diffuse fibrous subtype and underwent the Mesh release technique. CT demonstrated widespread fibrous septa without a central fibrous mass, and three-dimensional reconstruction revealed an interconnected, multi-planar fibrous network. The mean operative time was 64.6 ± 12.3 min, and the mean aspirate volume was 269.1 ± 40.9 mL. Good-to-excellent contour improvement was achieved in 90.8% of patients. Postoperative complications occurred in 23.1% of patients, including transient numbness and seroma. Conclusions Preoperative CT distinguishes localized and diffuse fibrous subtypes of fibrous-dominant dorsocervical humps. For the diffuse fibrous subtype, the Mesh release technique enables effective cross-plane disruption of the fibrous network while achieving favorable contour restoration. Level of evidence iv This journal requires that authors assign a level of evidence to each article. title: Addressing unilateral lambdoid craniosynostosis using endoscopic suturectomy and barrel-stave osteotomies: surgical technique and literature review.
abstract: Purpose Unilateral lambdoid craniosynostosis (ULC) is a rare cranial deformity requiring intervention to correct asymmetry of the posterior skull. Conventional open remodeling and distraction osteogenesis offer robust expansion but carry risks of higher blood loss, hardware complications, or reoperation. We report a novel, minimally invasive technique combining endoscopic lambdoid suturectomy with barrel-stave osteotomies, supplemented by a literature review. Case description A 2-month-old healthy male presented with classic left ULC features, including occipitoparietal flattening, ipsilateral mastoid bulge, contralateral parietal bulge, and ear level asymmetry, confirmed by 3D computed tomography. Under endoscopic guidance through two small incisions, a 10-cm-long by 1.2-cm-wide lambdoid suturectomy was performed. To enhance immediate intraoperative expansion, seven 3-cm barrel-stave osteotomies were placed perpendicularly along the superior (4 cuts) and inferior (3 cuts) suture margins and gently greenstick-fractured outward. The estimated blood loss was 10 mL without perioperative complications. Postoperative cranial molding helmet therapy was initiated on day 10. At the 4-month follow-up visit, 3D surface scanning demonstrated marked improvement in head shape and symmetry. Conclusions Our method, endoscopic suturectomy and barrel-stave osteotomies on a single patient with unilateral lambdoid craniosynostosis, demonstrated safe and favorable outcomes. We believe the addition of barrel-stave osteotomies to suturectomy may yield superior clinical outcomes, compared to conventional endoscopic-assisted procedures with suturectomy alone. However, it is necessary to accumulate a larger number of cases and conduct long-term follow-up studies to further validate this hypothesis.

title: Relative frequency of non-Wilms renal tumours in children: an institutional experience from a national tertiary referral centre in Malaysia.
abstract: Purpose International protocols for paediatric renal tumours are largely based on Western data with Wilms tumour (WT) accounting for more than 90% of cases. We aimed to evaluate the relative frequency of WT and Non-Wilms Renal Tumours (NWRTs) in a diverse Asian cohort in Malaysia. Methods A retrospective review was conducted of all primary paediatric renal tumours treated at a national tertiary referral centre from 2015 to 2024. Diagnosis was confirmed via post-operative histopathology. Results Of 95 children (median age 29 months), all were Asian descent (73.7% Malay, 9.5% Chinese, 6.3% Indian). WT accounted for only 68.4% of cases, while NWRTs accounted for 31.6%. Among NWRTs, 63.3% were malignant, primarily clear cell sarcoma of the kidney (CCSK, n = 7) and renal cell carcinoma (RCC, n = 4). In the classic WT age range (6-84 months), WT prevalence was only 75.6%, with CCSK representing 9.0%. Congenital mesoblastic nephroma (CMN) predominated in infants < 6 months (71.4%), while RCC was exclusively seen in children > 84 months (40.0%). Conclusion The substantial proportion of malignant NWRTs observed in this institutional cohort highlights potential risks of neoadjuvant chemotherapy without histological confirmation. Histopathological diagnosis via percutaneous core-needle biopsy or primary surgery may be highly considered in similar clinical settings.
